scoreNote: Strong (5): argues that questioning authority checks the abuse of power and drives progress, then qualifies that the well-being promised depends on reasoned, responsible questioning rather than reflexive defiance; well argued.

sentences.text: Every tyrant's favorite citizen is the one who never asks why.
The statement takes the opposite side, holding that a society's well-being is enhanced when many of its people question authority.

The statement is largely right, since the habit of questioning authority checks abuses and drives progress that obedience never could; but it holds only when the questioning is reasoned and responsible, not mere reflexive defiance.
A society is healthier when its people question authority because power left unquestioned tends to corrupt.
Rulers, officials, and institutions naturally drift toward serving themselves, and only a public willing to scrutinize and challenge them keeps that drift in check.
Where citizens question authority, corruption is exposed and tyranny resisted; where they do not, abuses go unchallenged until they harden into oppression.
A questioning public is the ultimate check on power, the force that makes leaders answerable and keeps them honest.
A free press, an active citizenry, and the courage to demand answers are what stand between a people and the abuse of their rulers.
By holding the powerful to account, widespread questioning protects a society from those who would misrule it.
Moreover, questioning authority is the engine of progress as well as the guardian against abuse.
Almost every advance in human knowledge and justice began when someone refused to accept the reigning dogma that authority had declared true.
Science advanced by doubting old certainties, and societies grew freer by questioning the right of kings, masters, and customs to command unthinking obedience.
A society where no one questions authority stagnates, repeating its errors because no one is permitted to point them out.
Those who challenged kings, priests, and slaveholders were called troublemakers in their day and are honored as liberators now.
Progress depends on people willing to ask whether what they are told is actually true or just.

sections.role: Body — But it must be reasoned

sentences.text: Still, the statement holds only when the questioning is thoughtful and responsible.
Questioning authority is valuable as a search for truth and justice, not as reflexive contrarianism that rejects every rule simply because it is a rule.
A society in which people reject all authority, including legitimate and necessary authority, descends not into freedom but into chaos and mutual distrust.
The well-being the statement promises comes from citizens who question in order to improve and hold to account, not from those who merely defy for its own sake.
The point is to question authority intelligently and in good faith, not to despise it indiscriminately.
It is reasoned questioning, aimed at truth and accountability, that enhances a society.
In conclusion, the statement is right that a society's well-being is enhanced when many of its people question authority.

Such questioning checks the abuse of power and drives the progress that obedience cannot, so it is genuinely good for a society, provided it is the reasoned, responsible questioning that seeks truth and accountability rather than the empty defiance that seeks only to reject.
Teach a people to question wisely, and you have given them the surest guard of their own freedom.
